title: Technology Sector Update for 09/07/2018: SGMS,CZR,HURC,FSNN,MTSL - Nasdaq.com
text:

Technology stocks extended their retreat Friday afternoon, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing over 0.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was slipped just over 0.4%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Scientific Games ( SGMS ) rose over 8% on Friday trading after the gaming technology developer said it launched mobile sports betting application with Caesars Entertainment ( CZR ) in New Jersey on Thursday to coincide with the start of the professional football season. The application allows Caesars customers in the state to place bets using their mobile devices and expands on Caesars' sportsbook betting. Sports betting became legal in New Jersey earlier this year following a U.S. Supreme Court decision knocking down most prohibitions on the activity.
In other sector news:
(+) Hurco ( HURC ) was almost 6% higher Friday afternoon, easing somewhat from a nearly 10% advance earlier in the session that followed the industrial technology reporting improved fiscal Q3 net income and sales compared with year-ago levels. The company earned $0.95 per share during the three months ended July 31, up from $0.58 per share during the same quarter last year, as sales and service fees grew to $78.8 million from $60.8 million during the May-to-July reporting period last year. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison.
(+) Fusion Telecommunications International ( FSNN ) rose almost 2% on Friday after saying it has received a $1.1 million, three-year contract to provide cloud services to an unnamed family entertainment center and restaurant chain. The new contract covers several hundred of the chain's restaurants throughout the United States, with Fusion adding the deal also is now reviewing a multiple-site deployment to the company's locations in Canada
(-) MER Telemanagement Solutions ( MTSL ) at one point Friday slumped almost 22% after the Israeli networking equipment company swung to a non-GAAP net loss of $0.25 per share during the six months ended June 30, reversing an adjusted 0.02 per share profit during the first six months in 2017. Revenue dropped 19.4% year over year during the period, falling to $2.9 million from $3.6 million during the six months ended June 20, 2017. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison.
